question: If the fit100 backbone is refit so that FIT, SELECT (early stop), CAL (temperature) and EVAL all use consistent prequential (strictly-prior per game date) 2026 history features, does prediction improve vs H0 (recorded fit100) and vs H2 (frozen fit100 + prequential EVAL features, EXP-WS-RECENCY-001)? Is the refit a candidate for a future serving SHADOW?
structural_note: FIT-row features are unchanged by construction (every FIT row's history was already strictly prior), so the deterministic LightGBM refit reproduces the same trees; arm P can differ from H2 only through the SELECT-chosen iteration (early stop on fresh SELECT features) and the CAL temperatures. Observed: parent iteration 162 vs 195 (model.txt differs), narrow_whiff 195 vs 195 (model.txt byte-identical), ground_ball 186 vs 191; temperatures parent 0.99415 vs 0.99460, narrow_whiff 0.95104 vs 0.94970, ground_ball 0.99189 vs 1.01522.

interpretation: The consistent prequential refit reproduces the E1 gain over the recorded fit100 (P-H0 NLL -0.00177, CI below zero; S0 pitchers -0.0061) but adds nothing over simply feeding the frozen fit100 prequential features (P-H2 -0.000003, CI [-0.0001, +0.0001]; Brier +0.00001). This is the expected outcome given the structural note: the trees are determined by FIT features that did not change, and only the early-stop iteration and the temperatures moved. Serving-shadow reading (pre-registered labels, never a winner): the refit is NOT a shadow candidate in its own right — the cheaper H2 configuration (existing fit100 model + nightly strictly-prior history refresh) is the candidate to carry forward; a classifier retrain is not required for this gain. What would be needed for a further gain is a change in model inputs or architecture (E4 sequence model), not more consistent history for the same trees. LIMITS: 2026 EXPOSED DEVELOPMENT; EVAL already exposed in scale-002/E1; one seed, one arm; 2026-only history; prequential features are a retrospective replay (live arrival timing unknown).
